value.rationale: The finite classification identifies a natural structural transition in synchronization-error list decoding: a list-two code of size 33 at n=7 exceeds the absolute union-of-two-unique-code upper bound 32, and exact shorter-length capacities prove seven is the first length where the capacity inequality holds. Unlike a routine tiny numerical improvement, this establishes indecomposability of two-list deletion codes relative to zero-error classes, and the complete L=1..8 profile gives an unambiguous natural finite benchmark. Does not assert asymptotic implications or unexplained practical improvements.
